name: Techspert
description: Techspert is an AI-powered expert network focused on healthcare and life sciences. It offers expert interviews, surveys, transcription and research analysis, alongside specialist support for healthcare AI model training and evaluation.
pricingDetail: Techspert says expert engagements are paid at a pre-agreed rate. Client pricing and expert pay ranges were not established from the public sources reviewed.
keyDifferentiators: Research tools for transcript analysis and data capture

compliance.expertVetting: Techspert says it checks identity, professional credentials, sanctions and regulatory history.

overview:
Techspert is an AI-powered expert network and primary research platform focused on healthcare and life sciences. Its company history dates its founding in Cambridge to 2016. The current site lists Cambridge as its HQ and London, Houston and Santiago as other offices.

Techspert reports over 25 million contactable healthcare experts, distinct from its 400,000-plus engaged experts. Its research services include interviews and surveys, supported by project managers and analysis tools. The company also offers healthcare specialists for AI model training and evaluation.

On 24 February 2026, Palatine Growth Credit announced £5 million in funding for hiring and AI research and market intelligence development. Hiring around 20 people during 2026 was a plan, not a confirmed completed expansion.

history.narrative:
Techspert was previously known as Biotechspert. Its 2020 funding announcement names Graham Mills and David Holden-White as founders in 2016 and describes working with CTO Hari Jackson on its AI technology.

Tech.eu reported a £1 million angel round in December 2018. A February 2020 announcement published by Martlet Capital reported a £3.76 million Series A led by Nauta Capital with Cambridge Angels participating. Techspert later announced a $12 million round led by BGF with Nauta Capital and reported opening a Houston office in 2021. In the 2021 announcement, the company described a knowledge graph covering millions of expertise areas.

timeline.event: Founded in Cambridge, according to company history.
Raised £1M from investors including Simon Thorpe, Angel CoFund and GW Asia Capital, reported by Tech.eu.
Announced £3.76M Series A led by Nauta Capital with Cambridge Angels participating.
Announced $12M investment led by BGF with Nauta Capital; reported opening Houston office.
Published an update on Data Capture, which structures call evidence into a research Q&A grid.
Palatine Growth Credit announced £5M funding for hiring and AI development.

servicesDetailed.name: AI-Powered Expert Search
servicesDetailed.description: Techspert describes using AI and machine learning to discover experts from online information and match them to research briefs.

servicesDetailed.name: Expert Consultations
servicesDetailed.description: One-on-one calls with subject matter experts; the current offering focuses on healthcare and life sciences.

servicesDetailed.name: Focus Groups & Data Review
servicesDetailed.description: Company materials describe multi-expert focus groups, data reviews and appraisals alongside one-off conversations.

servicesDetailed.name: Quantitative Surveys
servicesDetailed.description: Techspert offers paid online surveys. Its expert FAQs say rates are agreed before participation.

servicesDetailed.name: ECHO Ask
servicesDetailed.description: Techspert describes ECHO Ask as an assistant for querying individual or multiple call records, comparing respondent groups and finding supporting quotes.

servicesDetailed.name: Data Capture
servicesDetailed.description: The company describes converting call recordings and discussion guides into structured Q&A grids with supporting evidence, including recordings from other providers.

servicesDetailed.name: AI Model Training & Evaluation
servicesDetailed.description: Techspert offers clinicians for data annotation, expert-authored training examples and evaluation of healthcare model outputs.

aiPlatform.narrative: Techspert describes AI-assisted expert sourcing and transcript analysis. Its Data Capture workflow organizes interview responses for research teams. Company updates also describe opt-in MCP access to search historical qualitative and quantitative research from customers’ AI workspaces. These are company-described capabilities, not independently measured accuracy claims.
features: ECHO Ask analysis across call records
Customer MCP access to historical research

complianceExtended.narrative: Techspert states that its platform is HIPAA and GDPR compliant, provides project audit trails and uses identity, credential and sanctions checks. These are company statements rather than an independent compliance assessment. Its AI policy acknowledges possible bias and inaccuracies and asks users to validate results.
highlights: Company-stated adverse event handling training and fair market value payments
Company-stated encryption and role-based access controls
Company-stated restriction of AI to approved transcript and workflow data
Company says customer data does not train AI models

clientFit.narrative: Editorial fit assessment based on the published healthcare research offering: suited to teams seeking clinical and scientific expert input alongside transcript analysis.

strengths: Expert interviews and surveys alongside analysis tools
Specialist input for healthcare AI training and evaluation
caveats: Contactable profiles and engaged experts are different measures; company-reported reach is not a count of completed consultations.
The AI compliance statement warns of inaccuracies and bias and recommends validating results.
Client prices, expert pay ranges and current employee count were not established in the reviewed sources.
Public sources disagree on headquarters and working arrangements; confirm these with the provider.
notableFacts: Company materials now include customer MCP access and healthcare AI model training
Techspert says it partners with Ecologi on carbon offset and reforestation projects
